A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 37-page MCLC paper, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of all equations, tables, figures and appendix material.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original reconstruction experiments in Section 4, including FFHQ, ImageNet and AFHQ results, alongside ablations, artifact analyses and additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices, including quantitative reconstruction comparisons and qualitative artifact analyses.

M1.justification: The projected Langevin correction in Section 3 and its integration into solvers in Algorithms 1–6 are identical. No algorithm steps, components or inference procedures change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same datasets and tasks, including FFHQ, ImageNet, AFHQ, deblurring, super-resolution, inpainting, HDR reconstruction and the guided-generation example in Appendix C.4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the reported experiments. DiffStateGrad, MPGD and SILO remain in their corresponding comparisons, and the base-versus-MCLC experiments retain the same solvers.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B/D retain identical validation subsets, degradation settings, resolutions, metrics and solver budgets, including the 100-image main evaluations and the full 1,000-image FFHQ check.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the same measurement-consistency ablation, patch-granularity checks, default-hyperparameter tests, baseline step-size sweeps and blob-artifact analyses. Their evidence is unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical in both versions. No repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same FFHQ Gaussian-deblurring LDPS-MCLC results: PSNR 28.14, LPIPS 0.303, FID 80.83 and P-FID 54.74.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1, Proposition 3.2, Theorem 3.4 and all Appendix A proofs and derivations are identical, including the KL-divergence arguments and measurement-consistency bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain identical claims about characterizing solver instability and stabilizing inverse solvers through measurement-consistent Langevin correction.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including reduced effectiveness with LatentDAPS, hyperparameter-tuning requirements, persistent blob artifacts and the discussion of applicability to flow-based models.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hardware and runtime disclosures, implementation-source references and hyperparameters in Tables 11–14 are identical. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are identical, including comparisons with manifold-preserving methods and the distinction from predictor–corrector sampling in Appendix B.2.

P1.justification: On pages 2–37, v3 replaces 'Submission and Formatting Instructions for ICML 2026' with 'Measurement-Consistent Langevin Corrector'. The first-page preprint date and arXiv version/date stamp also update. Body wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–23 and Tables 1–14 retain identical displays, captions, formatting and placement. Page layout remains unchanged; the running-header wording correction does not reflow the document.

improvement.justification: Replacing the erroneous template running header with the paper's short title modestly improves document identification and presentation throughout the main text and appendices. The scientific argument, results and reproducibility information are identical, so the benefit is limited to editorial polish.
